decision: Choose a retrieval and review workflow that avoids losing candidate matches before scoring.
primary_outcome: Adjudicated true-match retrieval recall at candidate generation, followed separately by review precision and workload.
denominator: All independently adjudicated positive aliases for recall; all reviewed candidates for precision; historical zero scores are a different descriptive denominator.
independence_unit: Underlying entity; many aliases of one entity are not independent entities.
quality_guardrail: Missed-entity risk, reviewer capacity and no identity decision from string similarity alone.
minimum_data: Entity/alias IDs, source provenance, blocker and scorer versions, complete candidate sets, adjudicated identity and review time.
failure_handling: Unadjudicated negatives remain unknown. A zero blocked score may mean not retrieved, so compare retrieval sets before scoring quality.
release_rule: Require verified retrieval quality and bounded review load before operational use; historical alias scores alone do not validate compliance performance.
reversal: A broader blocker recovers missed positives but exceeds review capacity, or entity-held-out validation reveals retrieval loss.
status: PROPOSED MEASUREMENT CONTRACT; NOT AN EXECUTED DOMAIN EXPERIMENT
defense: Does 909 of 6,000 establish an impossibility limit?
No. It describes zero scores in one historical blocked pipeline. A fixture shows that prefix blocking can discard a high-similarity match.
A scorer cannot rescue a candidate it never receives. Measuring them separately identifies the operational cause of a miss.
